hotel_upper_salvage_arrival.speaker: hotel_salvage_clerk

text.desc: The stall rises through the ceiling hatch. You cling to its frame as the crane carries it into a storage mezzanine above the hotel.
It swings beside dismantled sinks, mirrors, and bathroom partitions. You climb onto the metal walkway.
The toilet is still inside the stall. Its plumbing has been disconnected, and the whole arrangement hangs several feet above the floor.
A salvage clerk approaches with a clipboard.

text.say: Plumbing isn't included in the lot.
I JUST WANT TO USE IT!

text.desc: He checks a box on his clipboard.
An open maintenance hatch leads toward the pipework. Service stairs descend toward the loading dock. Surely somebody knows where an installed toilet is.

choices.text: ASK WHERE AN INSTALLED TOILET CAN BE FOUND.
DESCEND THE SERVICE STAIRS TOWARD THE LOADING DOCK.

hotel_upper_salvage_arrival.notes: Owner approved B/C/D only. The manifest-inspection option A is explicitly retired. No new roll, item, or wedding task; crane d6 success is upstream.

hotel_upper_salvage_clerk_directions.speaker: hotel_salvage_clerk

text.say: WHERE CAN I FIND A TOILET THAT ISN'T BEING SOLD?
There's a staff lavatory one floor down.
It's still on the floor plan.
That's all the floor plan can tell you.

text.desc: He points toward the service stairs.

hotel_upper_salvage_clerk_directions.notes: Short owner-approved exchange. Connects to existing sold-for-storage staff lavatory; no replay of wedding introductions.

hotel_freight_wc_misunderstanding.speaker: hotel_lift_voice

text.desc: You step into the freight elevator. Its panel has three buttons. One is marked W.C. Finally.
You press it. The elevator rattles upward.
The doors open onto a storage mezzanine filled with dismantled sinks, toilets, and bathroom partitions.

text.say: THEN WHY DOES THE BUTTON SAY W.C.?
It was cheaper than replacing the panel.

text.desc: You step onto the mezzanine. A salvage clerk studies a clipboard nearby. An open maintenance hatch leads toward the pipework. The lift remains behind you.

choices.text: ASK THE SALVAGE CLERK WHERE A WORKING TOILET IS.
RIDE BACK DOWN AND LEAVE THE HOTEL.

hotel_freight_wc_misunderstanding.notes: Owner-approved final Chapter 4 editorial stop. W.C. means Warehouse Collection, not water closet. Reuses upstairs clerk and pipe routes without replaying hanging-stall arrival. No extra roll, fee, inventory, or wedding tasks.
